chunks: Ibn Masrur, from Muhammad al-Himyari, from his father, from Ibn Hashim, from al-Rayyan who said:
I said to al-Ridha (peace be upon him): What do you say about the Qur’an? He said: The Speech of Allah. Do not go beyond it nor search for guidance in other than it - for you will be led astray.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of the Qur'an and how should one seek guidance according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Tawhid*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) affirms the Qur’an as the uncreated Speech of Allah, establishing it as the exclusive source of divine guidance. This hadith underscores the Shia principle of *al-Insiraf* (turning away) from other sources when the Qur’an suffices, warning that deviation from its clear bounds leads to spiritual misguidance.

en.ammaar-muslim: [2/1574] Tawhid of al-Saduq and his Amali: Ibn Masrur from Muhammad al-Himyari from his father from Ibn Hashim from al-Rayyan who said:
I said to al-Ridha عليه السلام: What do you say about the Qur’an? He said: The Speech of Allah. Do not go beyond it nor search for guidance in other than it - for you will be led astray
